title: Retreating squad turns back as soon as it leaves engagement range (retreat hysteresis bypassed)
description: When nearby.Count == 0 the controller takes the `!order.Engage || nearby.Count == 0` branch and issues RouteCommand (attack-move toward the target) without consulting the squad's combat state. A squad in the Retreating state therefore turns around as soon as it is more than EngagementRangeCells (10) from the enemy's last-seen position. Back in range it is still Retreating, so it retreats again. The 0.6/1.0 thresholds and the 5 s MinStateSeconds never apply to this cycle, which breaks the squad hysteresis in invariant 3.
failure_scenario: Confirmed with a scratch xunit probe, since deleted. Setup: 2 tanks worth 1600 attacking; one armed enemy worth 5000 last seen at (50,51); squad positions alternate between 14 and 7 cells from it every 2 s. Commands observed: t=0 Move(home), t=2 AttackMove(target), t=4 Move, t=6 AttackMove, t=8 Move. The squad bounces at the edge of engagement range and bleeds units instead of disengaging.
suggested_fix: While state is Retreating, keep issuing RetreatCommand until re-engage conditions hold, even when no enemy is in range. Only a fresh engage evaluation (ratio > ReEngageAboveForceRatio after MinStateSeconds) or the squad reaching home should clear Retreating. Alternatively, clear it explicitly after a set time out of contact.

RouteCommand (lines 154-167) returns an AttackMoveCommand toward order.TargetRegion. The only way out of Retreating is at lines 87-90 (ratio > ReEngageAboveForceRatio && heldSeconds >= MinStateSeconds), and it runs only when nearby.Count > 0. OperationalPlanner.Squads.cs:88-160 re-issues the attack squad with the same target and Engage=true, and makes a retreat squad only for an intent ObjectiveKind.Retreat. title: Squad combat state is keyed by reused squad id and never cleared, so a new wave inherits a stale Retreating state
description: combatStates is keyed by SquadId. The planner reuses the fixed ids "attack", "defend", "retreat", "harass" and "scout" for every wave: it disbands the squad each pass and recreates it. GetOrInitState initialises from the local ratio only the first time an id is seen and never removes an entry. A later attack wave with entirely different units therefore starts in whatever state the last wave left. Since Since is minutes old, MinStateSeconds is already satisfied, and a Retreating state only clears above the 1.0 re-engage ratio.
failure_scenario: Confirmed with a probe. Wave 1 ("attack", units 1 and 2) meets ratio 0.32 at t=0 and gets Retreating (correct). Wave 2 ("attack", units 3 and 4) meets ratio 0.8 at t=300 s, above the 0.6 retreat line. Expected AttackCommand; actual MoveCommand (retreat). Every later attack in the 0.6-1.0 band is abandoned on contact, and the stale state also combines with the out-of-range turn-back bug above.
suggested_fix: Reset or drop a squad's combat state when its membership changes substantially or it has had no contact for N seconds. At minimum, prune entries whose squad id is absent from the current orders and key the state by a squad generation. Re-initialise from the current ratio when a squad first makes contact.

title: Repair lease has no hysteresis: units are handed back to the squad at 40% health
description: RepairController takes a vehicle's lease (priority 15 beats squad priority 10 once the squad's min hold has passed) when HealthFraction < 0.4. It stops renewing once HealthFraction >= 0.4, using the same threshold for exit as for entry. The lease lapses 3 s later; the next planner pass re-leases the unit to its squad, and the squad immediately attack-moves it. In RA2 that order pulls the unit off the repair pad, so it returns at about 40% health, drops below 0.4 again, and ping-pongs between repair and squad. The simulator hides this: its RepairRequested flag persists through move orders and heals without a depot.
failure_scenario: A tank at 0.39 HP near a depot is preempted by "repair" and gets a RepairCommand. At 0.41 HP the controller skips it and the lease expires. squad:attack reacquires it and issues AttackMove. The tank leaves the pad at about 41% HP, is damaged back below 0.4 within seconds, and the cycle repeats. Squads keep losing members to a repair loop that never restores them.
suggested_fix: Add an exit threshold, e.g. keep the lease until HealthFraction >= 0.9 or the unit is fully repaired. Renew whenever currentOwner == repair and HP is below the exit threshold, not the entry threshold.

title: Retreating squad attack-moves straight back into the fight as soon as it leaves engagement range (endless ping-pong)
description: The retreat/re-engage state is only evaluated when enemies are within EngagementRangeCells. Once a Retreating squad moves out of that 10-cell range, `nearby.Count == 0` sends it to RouteCommand, which attack-moves toward order.TargetRegion, which is the enemy position it just fled. It re-enters range, is still Retreating (ratio unchanged), and is sent home again. The planner keeps the attack squad alive while army >= 0.5*threshold, so this never resolves.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated with a scratch xUnit test in a scratch copy of HEAD, using real SquadController and armed rules. There is one 800-value tank ordered to AttackRegion Front, with an armed 4000-value enemy at (50,55). The commands alternate for 30+ seconds: MoveCommand (retreat) while at y=52, then AttackMoveCommand->(50,50) as soon as the tank reaches y=38 (out of range), then Move again, and so on. The squad shuttles at the range boundary taking fire and never fights or disengages.
suggested_fix: While a squad is Retreating, keep issuing the retreat move (or hold at the rally point) until the planner reassigns it or ReEngage conditions are met. Do not fall through to RouteCommand toward the attack target. Optionally have the planner treat a retreating attack squad as a regroup/staging request.

title: Defend squad at the base is ordered to Move (not fight) exactly when the base is overrun
description: OperationalPlanner.LeaseAndOrder gives every squad, including `defend`, the same RetreatBelowForceRatio (0.6). RetreatCommand sends units to the centre of the lowest-id region holding an own building, which is usually the base being defended. When a superior force hits the base (local ratio < 0.6), the defenders get a plain MoveCommand to their own base centre on every tactical tick instead of Attack/AttackMove. In RA2, units under a move order do not return fire until they arrive, and re-issuing the order each tick keeps them passive.
failure_scenario: The base region holds 1000 value of defenders when a 2000-value enemy wave arrives (ratio 0.5 < 0.6). After MinStateSeconds the defend squad switches to Retreating and receives MoveCommand(base centre) repeatedly, so the defenders stop engaging while the base is destroyed. There is also nowhere to retreat to.
suggested_fix: Do not apply retreat hysteresis to DefendRegion squads whose target is a base region (pass retreat ratio 0 for defend), or make retreat for a squad already at home an AttackMove/hold-position.

title: Scout and retreat squads (Engage=false) are routed with AttackMove, so they stop to fight
description: When `!order.Engage`, the controller calls RouteCommand, which always returns AttackMoveCommand. The planner creates the `scout` and `retreat` squads with engage:false precisely so they avoid combat. With attack-move, a lone scout engages every enemy it meets, and an army under an ObjectiveKind.Retreat objective fights its way home instead of disengaging.
failure_scenario: The intent carries a Retreat objective after losing a fight, and PlanSquads puts the whole army in `retreat` with engage:false. SquadController emits AttackMoveCommand toward home, so units that meet the pursuing enemy stop to shoot, and the retreat turns into a running fight. The fastest-unit scout likewise stops at the first enemy unit and dies instead of scouting.
suggested_fix: In RouteCommand, emit MoveCommand when order.Engage is false and AttackMoveCommand only when it is true.

title: Harvesters flee from unarmed enemy vehicles (enemy harvesters/MCVs), abandoning shared ore fields
description: combatContacts contains every infantry, vehicle and aircraft contact regardless of armament (no Weapon/Damage check, unlike SquadController.IsArmed). An enemy harvester, MCV or engineer within ThreatRangeCells counts as a threat, so the own harvester is sent back to the refinery. When the threat clears it is re-sent to the field and flees again, which costs income every time the two economies share an ore field.

On maps with a contested middle field the bot's harvesters cycle between flee and harvest whenever enemy miners are present.
suggested_fix: Filter combatContacts to armed types (rules.TryGet(...) && Weapon != None && Damage > 0). Also consider fleeing away from the threat rather than to the nearest refinery, which may lie past it.

title: Repair controller sends damaged vehicles to any Production/Support building and holds them forever
description: The depots are all own buildings with role Production or Support: the construction yard, barracks and war factory as well as the service depot (GADEPT/NADEPT is the only Support building in bindery-sim-approx.json). The nearest one, usually the yard or barracks, becomes the RepairCommand depot. The planner never builds a service depot unless a playbook tech goal names it. In RA2 only a service depot repairs vehicles, so the repair never happens. The unit stays under 40%, the repair lease (priority 15 > squad 10) is renewed every tick, and the vehicle is removed from all squads for the rest of the game. The sim hides this because ApplyRepair heals the unit in place anywhere, without a depot or movement, which also inflates arena results.
failure_scenario: An Allied bot with GAYARD, GAPILE and GAWEAP and no GADEPT has a tank at 35% health within 40 cells of the base. It gets RepairCommand(tank, depot = GAYARD/GAPILE) every tick. On the live adapter the tank never repairs and is never returned to a squad, and each damaged vehicle becomes permanent dead weight. In the sim it heals in place, so arena metrics overstate bot strength.
suggested_fix: Select depots only by an explicit repair capability (e.g. a role or flag for service depots) and do nothing when there is none. Make the sim require the unit to reach a depot. Optionally add a service depot to the building plan once the war factory exists and vehicles are in the composition.

title: Building placement has no failure memory: a rejected cell is retried forever and the building queue deadlocks
description: PlanPlacement chooses the cell with BuildPlacement.ChooseCell. That is a pure function of the centroid of own building positions, the bias and a 3-cell spacing check, with no footprint (Foundation) size, terrain, ore or unit-occupancy knowledge, and nothing records a failed placement. HasRoom(Building) returns false while the finished item waits for placement. If the engine rejects the cell (a 4x4 yard next to a 3-wide building 3 cells away, cliff, water, ore, a unit standing there), the next pass computes the identical cell and the building queue never advances. The sim cannot surface this because ApplyPlace accepts any cell within 24 cells of an own building.
failure_scenario: Live RA2: GAWEAP (3x5 footprint) finishes, and ChooseCell returns a cell 3 cells east of the construction yard's reported position, which overlaps the yard's foundation. place_building is rejected, the next second's plan issues the same PlaceBuildingCommand at the same cell, and so on. No further building, power or tech is ever built.
suggested_fix: Track rejected or unconfirmed placements per type and cell (the item is still ready N seconds after a PlaceBuildingCommand) and exclude those cells from the next search. Add footprint sizes to UnitRule and space by footprint. Make the sim reject overlapping footprints so the arena catches it.

title: Expand objective is ignored; 'expansion' refineries are always built at the main base
description: IntentComposer emits ObjectiveKind.Expand with an ExpansionCandidates region, and generic-expand/boom playbooks rely on expandAtSeconds. OperationalPlanner never reads ObjectiveKind.Expand: grep finds no consumer in Operations. RefineryTarget only raises the refinery count, and PlanPlacement places the refinery in the first free ring around the base centroid. The ore-field bias only chooses the side within a ring (the ring index is the primary sort in BuildPlacement), and it targets the field nearest the anchor, not the expansion region. No MCV is ever produced to expand either. The bot therefore never takes a second ore field; extra refineries crowd the home field and harvesters travel ever-longer trips once it depletes.
failure_scenario: The intent has posture Expand with Objective(Expand, r7) where r7 is a remote ore region. RefineryTarget becomes 2 at t >= expandAt, and the second GAREFN is placed at ring 1-2 around the home centroid (e.g. 3-6 cells away), not near r7. r7 is never occupied, and the ExpansionTaken event never fires from the bot's own action.
suggested_fix: When an Expand objective is present, place the next refinery (anchor and bias) at the objective region's ore field if it is within placement range of own buildings. Otherwise produce and escort an MCV there, or pick the nearest ore field without a refinery. At minimum, bias refineries toward ore fields that have no own refinery yet.

title: No barracks or army until ~6 minutes while floating 4-5k credits; single serial build order puts barracks last
description: NextBuilding orders power, then first refinery, then everything toward the harvester (war factory), then more refineries, composition and tech, then the power buffer, and only then 'extra production'. The barracks is reached only through the extra-production branch, and the defense queue is empty until then. The first infantry and the first defense only appear after the refinery and war factory have both finished. Meanwhile the starting cash sits unspent.
failure_scenario: Arena (scratch copy of HEAD, `run --arms selector --maps training --opponents turtle --seeds 1`, arm decision log): GAPOWR queued at 1s and placed at 49s, GAREFN placed at 171s, GAWEAP placed at 293s, and the first GAPILE queued at 329s. The first army unit (E1) was queued at 352s. Across 18 matches (rush/balanced/turtle x 3 maps x 2 seeds) the arm's averageCreditsOnHand ranged 2075-5361, mostly 3000-5000, and buildingsBuilt was 8 in 13 of 18 matches. A real early rush meets zero defenders for about 6 minutes.
suggested_fix: Insert the barracks (and a first defense when defense budget > 0) right after the first refinery, or whenever credits exceed the next building's cost by a margin. Treat idle credits above a threshold as a trigger to add production rather than requiring the power buffer first.

title: Planner flips attack/defend every pass around base threat 1.0, with no hysteresis or minimum time
description: Squad objective selection is level-triggered on `threat >= 1.0`. One operational pass (1 s) at or above 1.0 disbands the attack squad, sends the whole army to defend at the base and resets `attacking` to false. The next pass below 1.0 re-forms the attack squad toward the target, because the conditions still hold. The ratio is enemy value × confidence ÷ own army value. Contact confidence decays and jumps back on re-sighting, so a parked enemy group near the base moves the ratio back and forth across 1.0 again and again. Each flip also renames the squad (attack vs defend). That releases and re-acquires every unit lease, which restarts the 10 s squad min-hold, and gives the SquadController a different combat-state key. Invariant 3's hysteresis is applied to strategy and squad retreat but not to this operational switch.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated with a temporary planner test, since deleted. The intent has an AttackRegion(Front) objective and army value 2000. The base threat alternates each pass between 1980/2000 = 0.99 and 2020/2000 = 1.01. The squad orders were: attack->r2 | defend->r1 | attack->r2 | defend->r1 | attack->r2 | defend->r1. The army is re-routed across the map every second.
suggested_fix: Add hysteresis to the defend switch, as with AttackHoldFraction. Enter defend at 1.0 or above, leave it only below about 0.7, and require a minimum time in each state (for example the 5 s squad MinStateSeconds). Keep the squad id and leases stable across the switch.

title: Attack squad routing uses the mode region: a mob of fresh reinforcements pulls the front-line army back toward base
description: PlanSquads puts every pool unit, including units just built at base, into the single attack squad each pass (Fill). RouteCommand then sends one AttackMoveCommand for all held members to NextWaypoint(ModeRegion(members), target). When the units at base outnumber the units at the front, the mode region is Home. The waypoint then becomes the first hop out of Home, and the army already near the target is attack-moved backward to it. In the reverse case (mode = front), lone reinforcements at base are sent straight to the target region's centre and arrive one at a time. Either way the attack loses its front or feeds units in piecemeal.

SquadController.Tick emitted a single AttackMoveCommand with Destination (30,10), the Mid centre, for all 11 units. The tanks 18 cells from the target were ordered 22 cells back toward base.

title: Focus fire targets contacts last seen up to 20 s ago: the squad halts on ghosts, and in the sim chases their true, hidden position
description: `freshEnemies` accepts any contact with LastSeenAt within MaxContactAgeSeconds (20 s), and both the engagement test (`nearby`) and ChooseFocusTarget use that list. The ghost also enters the local force ratio and can trigger a retreat from nothing. In RA2 an attack order on an object outside vision is invalid or ignored. In the sim, ApplyAttack looks the target up by id among all live entities and paths to `target.Region`, its true current region. The squad therefore chases the unit through fog, an omniscient pursuit the belief does not justify.
